analysis.title: BofA Securities Equity Client Flow Trends: Big TMT stock outflows, dividend/quality ETF inflows
key_insights: BofA clients sold US equities for a 2nd week in the week of 10/19-10/23 (S&P 500 -0.5%). Single stock net sales were -$3.5bn after record ~$15bn outflows the prior week. Clients bought equity ETFs ($2.3bn) for the 2nd straight week.

Selling was driven by retail (private) clients, in their 2nd week of outflows (-$3.05bn stocks+ETFs, -$3.85bn single stocks). Hedge fund clients also sold (-$28mn total, -$431mn single stocks). Institutional clients bought (+$1.9bn total, +$757mn single stocks) after outsized tax loss selling earlier in October.
Clients sold equities across size segments on a stocks+ETFs basis: large cap -$81mn, mid cap -$736mn, small and micro cap -$319mn. Large cap single stock net sales were -$2.2bn.

Corporate client buybacks accelerated for the 4th week but are slightly below seasonal averages. YTD annualized buybacks are tracking below 2024-25 levels but above 2010-23 annual levels. Rolling 52-week buybacks as a % of S&P 500 market cap are the lowest since Aug. 2021 (0.18%, down from a 0.42% peak in Feb. 2025).

Comm. Svcs. had its biggest weekly outflow in its history as a GICS sector (since 9/2018), also the biggest when normalized by market cap (-$4.8bn single stocks, z-score -5.48 vs 5 years). It was the worst-performing sector last week amid a big post-results sell-off in Meta.

Industrials had the next-largest outflows (-$1.2bn single stocks), the 13th consecutive week of outflows. The longest streak on record is 30 weeks in 2016. Tech (-$931mn single stocks) and Utilities (-$267mn) also saw outflows.
7 of 11 sectors saw inflows. Consumer Discretionary led (+$1.1bn single stocks, biggest inflows since late Aug), followed by Financials (+$1.07bn, biggest since late July) and Health Care (+$1.0bn).

Clients bought ETFs across Value/Blend/Growth styles and across large, mid and small cap except broad market. Tech ETFs had the largest sector ETF inflows (+$317mn) after outflows over the prior four weeks (4-wk avg -$202mn).

Dividend ETF 4-wk avg flows hit a nearly 1-year high and Quality/Multi-Factor ETF flows reached their highest level in BofA's ETF history since Aug. 2025. BofA ties the rotation out of Momentum and into Value/Cash Return strategies to easing rates and rising AI concerns.
Rolling 4-wk avg US equity flows (single stocks + ETFs) stand at -$5.0bn. Total single stock flows 4-wk avg is -$6.35bn against a 52-wk avg of -$2.57bn.
Hedge fund clients are net buyers over the past 12 months, while institutional clients typically peak their selling in October versus retail in Nov/Dec.

YTD 2026 flows: single stocks -$98.1bn (hedge funds +$17.5bn, institutional -$63.2bn, private -$52.4bn) versus equity ETFs +$63.1bn. Clients are selling single stocks and buying equity ETFs this year.

Sector flow streaks in single stocks 4-wk avg: Energy outflows for 7th straight week, Financials 6th, Utilities 6th, Tech 4th, Comm. Svcs. 2nd, Health Care 2nd. Staples inflows for 3rd straight week, and Consumer Discretionary flipped positive.
earnings_insights: Meta had a big post-results sell-off last week, which BofA links to the record Comm. Svcs. outflow and the sector being the worst performer (refers to BofA's Earnings Tracker report).

macro_indicators.interpretation: The index fell modestly while clients net sold single stocks and bought ETFs.

risk_factors: Weekly flow data can be influenced by block trades and is more volatile than the 4-week average.
Retail single stock selling and record Comm. Svcs. outflows following big post-earnings moves (Meta) could continue.
Rising AI concerns are cited as a driver of rotation out of Momentum.
charts_described: Exhibit 3 plots rolling 4-wk avg net buying of Dividend and Quality/Multi-Factor ETFs from 8/2025 to now, with Dividend flows at a nearly 1-year high and Quality/Multi-Factor at the highest in BofA's ETF history since Aug. 2025.
Exhibit 21 shows rolling 52-week corporate client buybacks as a % of S&P 500 market cap peaking at 0.42% in Feb. 2025 and declining to 0.18%, the lowest since 2021.
Exhibit 19 compares BofA corporate clients' 4-week avg buybacks (YoY) with S&P 500 quarterly buybacks (YoY), at +102% YoY.
vol_and_positioning: Client single stock selling was -$3.5bn last week after record ~$15bn outflows the prior week. Selling was led by retail clients, with hedge funds also net sellers.

Rolling 4-wk avg total US equity flows are -$5.0bn. Institutional 4-wk avg single stock flows have been outflows for 5 straight weeks, and large cap single stock 4-wk avg outflows for 5 straight weeks.
Hedge fund 4-wk avg single stock flows were outflows for a 2nd straight week, while hedge fund total equity (stock+ETF) flows have been inflows since early August.

Corporate buybacks are slightly below seasonal averages and rolling 52-wk buybacks are the lowest as a % of market cap since Aug. 2021. Over the last 12 weeks, buybacks were highest in Financials ($7.1bn) and Tech ($4.7bn).
Dividend ETF inflows are at a nearly 1-year high on a 4-wk avg basis, and Quality/Multi-Factor ETF inflows are the highest in BofA's ETF history since Aug. 2025.
